descriptions.text: First major hack of 2026, as TrueBit was drained for $26.2 million through an overflow in unverified bytecode. The same attacker hit Sparkle weeks prior. Old code keeps bleeding - the archives have clearly become a shopping list.

The Truebit bonding-curve pool prices TRU purchases via getPurchasePrice(), computed roughly as (200*amount*reserve*T + 100*amount^2*reserve) / (100*T^2 - parameter*T^2). The attacker chose a buy amount (solving the curve so (amount+T)^2 exceeds the safe range) that drove the numerator/denominator math past the boundary where the purchase price effectively underflows toward zero (or wraps), letting them mint a huge quantity of TRU for a negligible amount of ETH. They then immediately sellTRU() back into the pool at the legitimate sell price, extracting ETH. Looping this buy-cheap / sell-rich cycle drained the pool of ~8540 ETH. The core defect is that the pricing formula was not bounded/validated against extreme amount and totalSupply values, so an attacker-selected input produces an arithmetically valid but economically nonsensical (near-zero) purchase price. Vulnerable code snippet: Attack Tx: https://etherscan.io/tx/0xcd4755645595094a8ab984d0db7e3b4aabde72a5c87c4f176a030629c47fb014 Analysis: https://www.certik.com/zh-CN/resources/blog/truebit-incident-analysis
The blockchain verification protocol Truebit was suspected to have been hacked, losing 8,535 ETH, valued at approximately $26.44 million.

On January 8, 2026, Truebit Protocol's Purchase contract was exploited through an unchecked integer overflow in its token pricing logic. Attackers supplied extremely large values to manipulate the calculation, minting massive TRU tokens for negligible ETH and immediately draining ~8,535 ETH (~$26.4M) from the contract. The protocol was running unaudited, legacy Solidity code without overflow protection, and no funds were recovered. The Purchase contract's getPurchasePrice() function calculated ETH prices for TRU tokens using arithmetic operations on user-supplied and contract state values. A bug in a smart contract belonging to the Ethereum-based Truebit project allowed an attacker to steal 8,535 ETH (~$26.4 million). The thief targeted one of the project's older contracts — deployed in 2021 — which contained a bug in which the price calculation to mint sufficiently large quantities of the protocol's TRU token would overflow , erroneously allowing people to mint large amounts of TRU for next to nothing. The exploiter took advantage of this by minting TRU and swapping it for ETH, ultimately causing the TRU token price to crash 99.9%. Another subsequent attack saw around $300,000 more drained from the project. Truebit acknowledged the hack…
